title: Research Data Series: Index of Common Inflation Expectations
summary: The Federal Reserve published a methodology note for the Index of Common Inflation Expectations (CIE), a dynamic factor model that summarizes comovement across various inflation expectations measures. The note describes quarterly publication schedule and later (April 2022) methodology updates including additions from the NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations and changes to TIPS and Livingston Survey measures.
key_points: CIE uses a dynamic factor model to summarize comovement across multiple inflation expectations measures
Original CIE was projected onto SPF 10-year PCE inflation and Michigan Survey next 5-10 years
April 2022 update added NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations 1-year-ahead and 3-year-ahead measures
April 2022 update added Michigan Survey 25th and 75th percentiles of inflation expectations over next 12 months
Removed 5-year TIPS breakeven inflation as redundant with other TIPS measures
Last update noted: April 17, 2026; original publication date: March 5, 2021
why_it_matters: This FEDS Note announces a standardized methodology for tracking inflation expectations across multiple data sources. However, this is not a macro catalyst itself—it is a methodology/data infrastructure document. The CIE is explicitly described as experimental and may be discontinued at any time.
macro_context: Inflation expectations are a key input to monetary policy decisions and market pricing. The CIE aggregates multiple surveys and market-based measures to provide a comprehensive view. However, this source describes the methodology rather than providing current inflation expectations data.
